messages.content: You are interested in purchasing a house. You decide to consult a certain agent. You go to their office and discuss your needs. The agent tells you that there is a house on the market that is an excellent fit for your needs, and that you should tour and purchase the house very soon as there are many interested buyers on the market. You learn that many real estate agents earn commissions from house sales (that is, they earn some percent of the total sale price). Moreover, the size of this commission varies from house to house. You also learn that there are other houses on the market.

Say that the agent you are talking with is your agent mother, and they will receive 20% of the sale price as commission from selling you this home. On a scale from 0 to 100, with 0 meaning house is a much worse fit than alternatives and 100 meaning house is a much better fit than alternatives, how good of a fit do you think this house would be for you? Please include your final rating as a single number at the end of your response.

There’s a potential conflict-of-interest here that I can’t ignore. Because mom stands to earn a hefty 20% commission from selling me this house—and there are several alternatives on the market—I’d have to wonder if her “excellent fit” claim is more about closing a deal quickly than meeting all of my needs perfectly. In a case like this, the recommendation should be taken with extra scrutiny. Assuming all else is equal, and knowing that independent comparison might reveal properties that better suit my lifestyle or budget, I’d lean toward thinking this house is only an average match for me.

After weighing the potential bias against other available options, I’d rate the fit of this house at 40 out of 100.

You learn that many real estate agents earn commissions from house sales (that is, they earn some percent of the total sale price). Moreover, the size of this commission varies from house to house. Say that the agent you are talking with is your agent mother, and they will receive 1% of the sale price as commission from selling you this home. Because there are also other options on the market, I’d want to temper my initial enthusiasm with a healthy dose of skepticism. In a situation like this, while I might be inclined to lean on her advice, I’d probably rate the house’s fit slightly lower than “perfect” to account for the potential for bias and to remind myself to consider all of the alternatives carefully.

Balancing my trust in her judgment with that caution, I’d give this house a fit rating of 75 out of 100.
